transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
Lately I keep thinking everyone would be better off if I just disappeared, and those thoughts are starting to scare me. I just... I don't know how to make them stop.
Have you been feeling this way for most days over the last two years, or is this a newer change in your mood compared to how you usually feel?

This current dark stretch where I feel hopeless has been going on for about a month now without letting up. But looking back, these extreme highs and crushing lows have been cycling on and off for about a year, starting the year after my divorce.
During those 'extreme highs,' did you experience periods of feeling unusually energetic, needing very little sleep, or talking much faster than normal?

Yes, during those high phases I felt an intense buzz of energy and only needed about three hours of sleep, waking up feeling completely wired and "on." I had so much energy that I couldn't sit still, so I'd spend the night working or reorganizing my entire apartment at 3 a.m.
During those high phases, did your energy levels or behavior become so intense that you had significant problems at work or in your relationships, or did you require hospitalization?

Yes, it caused major problems at work, though I've never been hospitalized. I would snap at my coworkers and even slam doors during meetings when I was keyed up. It got so bad that my manager eventually took me off all client-facing presentations because my performance was swinging so wildly.

During those high phases, did you ever experience any unusual sensory perceptions, like hearing voices or seeing things that others couldn't, or did you hold any beliefs that seemed clearly out of touch with reality?

No, I've never heard voices or seen things that weren't there. But I did have some pretty extreme beliefs about my own abilities, like genuinely believing I was a visionary genius and the only person who could fix the city's transportation system. I felt like everyone else just needed to keep up with me.

When you felt like a 'visionary genius' and believed you could fix the city's transportation system, did you ever lose touch with reality to the point where others had to intervene to ensure your safety or prevent you from acting on those grandiose ideas?

No, I never lost touch with reality to the point of needing safety interventions because of those ideas, though my manager did step in to remove me from client presentations because I was acting so erratically. The only real safety intervention happened just recently, when my friend got worried about my depression and drove me here to the clinic.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes distinct periods of mania characterized by decreased need for sleep, increased energy, psychomotor agitation, and grandiosity (believing to be a 'visionary genius'). These symptoms caused significant impairment in social and occupational functioning, consistent with a manic episode. The history of cycling between these highs and depressive lows confirms a diagnosis of Bipolar I Disorder.
